public_rationale: The March SelfCheckGPT study found that only 24.3% of 526 generated biographical sentences were accurate under its annotation scheme. That is strong evidence against treating those model outputs as standalone factual authorities. Contemporary external-source integrations show that LLMs could still contribute to factual applications. The supported conclusion concerns reliance on generated assertions alone, not every model-assisted information system.
limitations: The outcome depends on the ordinary standalone-authority reading of basis for factuality.
The numerical result is specific to text-davinci-003 and the sampled biography task.
The original study was a preprint when Marcus posted.
The evidence does not establish that LLMs were worse than every alternative information source.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are a very poor basis for factuality.

statement.excerpt: I personally haven't changed; I still think that LLMs are unreliable, and still think that they are a very poor basis for factuality.

from_speaker: a very poor basis for factuality
our_interpretation: The ordinary practical reading is that LLM-generated assertions were not dependable standalone factual authorities.
Very poor supplies no numerical cutoff. The assessment concerns material factual fabrication, not whether models sometimes answer correctly.
The claim does not automatically extend to an entire system that checks model output against external sources.
The current-state assessment uses March 1–30, 2023, the publication month through the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations show substantial factual fabrication in ordinary knowledge-generation tasks, undermining reliance on generated text alone.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary evaluations show dependable standalone factual generation across ordinary knowledge tasks, with fabrication sufficiently rare to support routine unchecked reliance.

evidence.excerpt: Of the 526 annotated sentences, 240 (45.7%) of the sentences were labelled major-inaccurate, 158 (30.0%) were minor-inaccurate, and 128 (24.3%) were accurate.
evidence.publisher: Potsawee Manakul, Adian Liusie and Mark J. F. Gales, University of Cambridge; arXiv
evidence.explanation: The original March report evaluates GPT-3 text-davinci-003 on 65 generated biographical passages and finds substantial factual fabrication. These are task-specific measurements, not an error rate for all LLM answers.

evidence.excerpt: We’re working with partners to integrate Claude with sources of solid, real-time information, like those found in search engines such as DuckDuckGo.
evidence.explanation: External-source integration was already a practical approach to factual applications. This limits any broader reading that LLMs could not contribute to factual systems, but supplies no measured accuracy establishing dependable standalone generation.
